fatal_errors: The proposed method is spark plasma sintering, whereas the target method is liquid-metal dealloying by immersion of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu.
The initial material is incorrectly treated as a mixed RHEA–Cu powder rather than an as-cast WTaVTi precursor with sacrificial Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels.
The mechanism of kinetically suppressing diffusion and segregation does not reconstruct the selective Ti–Cu exchange, retention of W/Ta/V ligaments, or formation of a W-rich passivating interlayer.
No evidence supports the claim that SPS produces a thermodynamically stable, homogeneous RHEA–Cu microstructure despite positive mixing enthalpy.
The predicted outcomes omit the directional bicontinuous architecture, enhanced high-temperature thermal conductivity, and qualified helium-irradiation response central to the target.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the general RHEA–Cu incompatibility and offers a testable comparison against conventional sintering, but it reconstructs neither the method nor the scientific rationale of the target. The target exploits pre-existing directional segregation through liquid-metal dealloying at 1200 °C for 96 h, selectively replacing Ti-rich channels with Cu and forming a stabilizing W-rich interface. SPS instead attempts to freeze a homogeneous powder-derived structure by limiting diffusion; this may provide transient kinetic refinement but does not establish long-term interfacial stability. The proposed experiment could test SPS homogeneity and mechanical properties, yet it does not measure thermal transport, interface chemistry, penetration scale, or irradiation behavior and provides no supporting evidence.
